edits.old:
Use this checklist when a person, advertisement, ideology, spiritual teaching, romantic pull, or inner voice is pressing too hard.

“I notice influence is happening. I do not need to obey it or attack it. I can slow down. I can ask what is being presupposed. I can ask who benefits. I can notice what my body is signaling without assuming what it proves. I can ask what love, truth, humility, and ordinary life would require.

If this is true, it will survive questions. If this is love, it will survive boundaries. If this is guidance, it will survive sleep. If this is for me, it will not require me to abandon my adult self.”

Before acting, ask:

Is there urgency?

Is there secrecy?

Is there shame?

Is there a threat of exclusion?

Is there a promise of specialness?

Is there sexual charge?

Is there spiritual superiority?

Is there a demand for money, sex, loyalty, silence, or obedience?

Is there a narrowing of choices?

Is questioning treated as betrayal?

Is resistance pathologized?

Is ordinary life being downgraded?

Is the child part being seduced, scared, or rescued?

Is the adult self still allowed to say no?

Several yes answers mean slow down. Don’t deepen trance or make an irreversible decision. Return to the room, body, food, sleep, time, and counsel.

A good guide increases your adult self. A bad guide replaces it. A good guide can tolerate your no. A bad guide calls your no resistance, ego, fear, low vibration, trauma, sin, or proof that you need more of their guidance.
edits.new:
Use this checklist when something is pressing on you too hard, whether it’s a person, an ad, an ideology, a spiritual teaching, a romantic pull or a voice inside you, stuff like that.

You could say something like, “Okay, I notice that I’m being influenced. I don’t have to obey it, and I don’t have to attack it either. I can slow down and ask what it’s taking for granted, and who it benefits. I can notice what my body is telling me and hold off on deciding what that proves. And I can ask what love, truth, humility and ordinary life would need from me here.

If it’s true, it can handle my questions. Real love can handle my boundaries, and real guidance will still be there after I sleep on it. And something that’s really for me won’t ask me to give up my adult self.”

Before acting on it, look for the usual signs, like urgency, secrecy, shame, a threat that you’ll be left out or a promise that you’re special, that kind of thing. Watch for a sexual charge too, or spiritual superiority. Be wary if it demands money or sex from you. Demands for your loyalty or your silence are signs too, and so is any demand for obedience.

It’s a warning if your choices keep getting narrower. Same if asking questions gets treated as betrayal, or your resistance gets treated like a pathology. Or if ordinary life starts to look small next to it.

Notice whether your child part is being seduced or scared. Being rescued can be part of it too. And check whether your adult self is still allowed to say no.

If you see several of these, slow down. Don’t go deeper into trance, and don’t make a decision you can’t undo. Come back to the room and your body, eat, sleep, give it time, get some counsel and so on.

You can tell a good guide because your adult self gets stronger with them, and they can take your no. A bad guide tries to replace your adult self. They’ll call your no resistance, ego, fear, low vibration, trauma, sin, you name it, and they’ll say it proves you need more of their guidance.

edits.diagnosis: question 2, c (Joel, 17:56): the general list of fourteen questions becomes three short paragraphs of prose (every sign kept, as statements in different shapes; where a list is needed it ends on a catch-all, his move, E125), and the lines around it are said plainly: the opening line leads with "pressing on you too hard"; the statement to say gets the guide's own lead-in ("You could say something like," as in "Love doesn't have to wait for trust") and plain words ("taking for granted" for "presupposed"); its four tests keep their pairs (truth and questions, love and boundaries, guidance and sleep, what is for me and the adult self) in four different shapes; the good and bad guide in two sentences instead of four parallel ones. The hypnosis-specific audit and its last line stay as published

edits.diagnosis: the inner-adult sweep (fix-20261021/CONFLATION-SWEEP.md, finding 1; Joel, 17:56: "check the guide for that conflation"): the script comes right after the paragraph on the inherited parent, which ends on "this voice may jump in to say that what you're doing is “fake”", so "I notice you" reads as said to that voice, and the lines after it ("if you stopped protecting me", "they don't have to stop protecting you") then hand the inherited parent the protector's job and leave to carry on. The published script said it to the protector ("You are trying to protect something"). Three words name who it's said to, a stage direction like the script's own "(Now talk to the protector."; the closing quotation mark that was missing goes in

edits.new: bring in a “Nurturer”, “Protector”, “Leader”, etc to help you

edits.diagnosis: the inner-adult sweep (fix-20261021/CONFLATION-SWEEP.md, finding 2; Joel, 17:56: "check the guide for that conflation"): the sentence before says "If you can identify any “protector” parts, talk to them", in the same lowercase, quoted form, so "bring in a “protector”" reads as one more of those guards. The published text and the rest of the guide give the three roles capitals. Capitals only

edits.old: It could also be an inner voice of a parent that you are picking up, and it is trying to enforce a rule about how you should be to belong to them. Again, it isn't useful to argue with this part, but find out what rule it is enforcing and then work on finding some ordinary evidence to build a more believable 'grown up' voice.
edits.new: It could also be the voice of your inherited inner parent that you are picking up, and it is trying to enforce a rule about how you should be to belong to them. Again, it isn't useful to argue with this part, but find out what rule it is enforcing and then work on finding some ordinary evidence to build a more believable 'grown up' voice of your own.
edits.published: The voice may be the inherited parent enforcing an old belonging rule. Don’t argue with it. Ask which rule it is enforcing and what ordinary evidence would make the new adult voice more believable.
edits.diagnosis: the inner-adult sweep (fix-20261021/CONFLATION-SWEEP.md, finding 3; Joel, 17:56: "check the guide for that conflation"), the pattern Joel fixed in "When “your voice” is everybody else’s voice": the parent's voice was just named, so "a more believable 'grown up' voice" can read as a more convincing version of that same voice (a parent is a grown-up whose voice you picked up). The published text says "the new adult voice". Two changes, as in his fix: his name for the internalized voice, "inherited inner parent", and "of your own" for the adult one
